summary: This photocatalytic depolymerization reaction utilizes a single electron transfer mechanism with perylene diimide (PDI) as the photocatalyst at 2.5 mol% loading. The process operates in a continuous-flow micro-reactor with 1.0 mm internal diameter tubing at 25°C using acetonitrile as solvent and DIPEA as base, with illumination from a xenon lamp at 420 nm wavelength. The flow process achieves remarkable intensification with a residence time of only 1.25 minutes compared to 8 hours (480 minutes) required in batch, representing a 384-fold time reduction while simultaneously improving yield from 95% to 99%. The dramatic improvement in flow results from enhanced light penetration and mass transfer in the micro-reactor format, enabling complete conversion in a fraction of the time required for batch processing.

summary: This photoredox catalysis involves a single-electron oxidation/fragmentation/cyanide trapping mechanism using Ir(dF(CF3)ppy)2(dtbbpy)PF6 as the photocatalyst in methanol at 60°C. The flow system utilized a 1.34 mL photochemical reactor with visible light irradiation and achieved a 96% yield with only a 2-minute residence time. In comparison, the batch process required 3 hours to reach 93% yield under otherwise identical conditions. Flow processing provided a dramatic 90-fold intensification factor by reducing reaction time from 180 minutes to 2 minutes while simultaneously improving yield by 3 percentage points. The continuous flow approach also offered enhanced safety through reduced solvent inventory and better heat management for the photochemical transformation.

summary: This study describes a photocatalyzed aerobic oxidation using 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole as the photocatalyst at 10 mol% loading. The reaction was conducted at 25°C with a 2-minute residence time in acetonitrile solvent using 420 nm LED irradiation. The flow setup employed a fixed-bed reactor (FBR) with 6 mm ID borosilicate glass tubing, 6 mL reactor volume, and 0.2 mL/min flow rate with a back pressure regulator at 1 bar. The flow process achieved 97.2% yield compared to 99% in batch, demonstrating nearly equivalent performance with significantly reduced reaction time from the batch baseline. The flow approach enabled precise control over residence time and continuous processing while maintaining high efficiency for this photocatalytic transformation.
